Hi Lisa / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on the procurement side:

Summary of call:
- Acme is evaluating Redwood to power internal search and chat experiences for a pilot (approx. 200k tokens/month initially).
- Primary success metrics: latency under 300ms tail, and cost predictability for Q2 pilot.

Procurement & commercial questions we discussed (please confirm):
1) Payment method: do you prefer PO or corporate card for initial purchase? If PO, any standard T&Cs or a procurement portal we should use?
2) Marketplace: you mentioned AWS Marketplace is an option for faster procurement — is that preferred by legal/procurement?
3) Procurement timeline: target signing window and any approval gates we should know about (e.g., finance review, legal SLA exceptions)?
4) Budget & approvers: who is the economic buyer and the finance sponsor we should loop in? Also who signs the contract?

Attachments: attaching a short SOW template and our standard PO contact info to help speed review.

Next steps:
- Lisa/Tom: confirm preferred payment method and marketplace interest + introduce budget owner or finance sponsor (name & email).
- Rafael (cc): I’ll share estimated pricing bands for PO vs card once we confirm payment path.
- I’ll follow up with a one-page commercial summary for procurement.

Thanks — talk soon.

—

Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement path & approvals - Acme Corp

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and the SOW. A few clarifications from procurement: 

1) Payment method: For pilots under $50k we typically use corporate card. Anything over that goes via PO. For multi-quarter commitments or annual contracts we'd need a PO.
2) Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is preferred for speed, but Legal needs to approve the contract language. If you can provide a Marketplace listing or AMI details we can fast-track it.
3) Timeline: Procurement can turn around PO paperwork in ~2 weeks once the budget owner signs off. Legal review (contract terms) typically takes 2–4 weeks depending on custom terms.
4) Budget & approvals: Economic buyer for this use case is likely Sarah Kim (VP Product) — I’ll introduce separately. Finance sponsor is Michael Grant (Director, Finance) — cc'ing procurement who can connect you. The signatory is our CFO for contracts >$100k; otherwise Sarah can sign for pilot purchases within delegated authority.

I’ve attached our PO template for your legal team.

Lisa Chen
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
lisa.chen@acme.com

Thanks Marissa / Lisa for the clarity. Quick internal alignment and suggested approach: 

Mapping the approval path (based on Lisa's note):
- Economic buyer: Sarah Kim (VP Product) — owns the initiative and budget.
- Finance sponsor: Michael Grant (Director, Finance) — will approve PO and cost center allocation.
- Signatory: CFO for >$100k; Sarah or delegated signatory for pilot-level purchases under $100k.

Commercial options to propose:
A) Fast pilot via AWS Marketplace / card payment (<$50k): fastest path, minimal legal review if using standard marketplace terms.
B) PO route (preferred for multi-quarter pilots or when Acme needs invoice terms): PO + standard Redwood master services agreement (MSA).
C) Reserved capacity / committed spend (if they want predictability) — requires more procurement lead time and billing setup.

Action items: 
- Marissa: ask Lisa to make an intro to Sarah + Michael so we can confirm authority and budget line.
- I’ll prepare two short commercial options (Marketplace/card and PO pricing) with expected timelines and a one-page comparison.
- Vivek: can help with any escalation for procurement/legal questions.

I'll draft the pricing note by EOD tomorrow.
